name: Enzyme Kinetics, Michaelis-Menten Analysis and Reversible Inhibition

reference.source: Harper's Illustrated Biochemistry / Medical Biochemistry 5th ed
clinicalPearls: Km represents substrate concentration at half-maximal velocity (Vmax/2); small Km indicates high enzyme-substrate affinity
Hexokinase has low Km (<0.1 mM) and is inhibited by G6P; glucokinase has high Km (~10 mM), acts as a glucose sensor and lacks G6P inhibition
On Lineweaver-Burk plots, y-intercept equals 1/Vmax, x-intercept equals -1/Km, and slope equals Km/Vmax
Competitive inhibitors increase apparent Km without changing Vmax; overcome by high substrate concentrations
Noncompetitive inhibitors decrease Vmax without changing Km; cannot be overcome by excess substrate
reference.pathophysiology: Enzymes stabilize reaction transition states to accelerate reaction rates by many orders of magnitude. Saturation kinetics reflect finite catalytic site availability. Reversible inhibitors alter apparent affinity or catalytic turnover, forming the basis of targeted pharmacotherapy (e.g., statins competing for HMG-CoA reductase). Allosteric effectors induce cooperative sigmoidal kinetics.
additionalDifferentials: Competitive vs noncompetitive vs uncompetitive pharmacological inhibition
Glucokinase deficiency (MODY2 mild fasting hyperglycemia) vs hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia
Heavy metal toxicity (lead noncompetitive inhibition of ferrochelatase and ALA dehydratase)
